title: Agent Builder's Playbook — Oct 6, 2026
intro: Verify before you trust: this week's cards cover checking graders, replays and baselines, and capping spend and untrusted inputs.

cards.title: Set a hard spend cap on every agent that calls a paid API
cards.problem: A looping or runaway agent on pay-per-use APIs can burn an unbounded bill before anyone notices.
cards.apply: Enforce a hard per-run and per-day spend ceiling at the gateway or key level, so the call is refused at the cap instead of alerting after the fact.
cards.result: A runaway loop costs at most the cap, not the month's budget.

evidence.note: Editorial argument from the source; no measured figure.

cards.title: Verify large agent refactors with a replay harness, not just tests
cards.problem: Agents can rewrite hundreds of thousands of lines, and unit tests alone do not prove behavior is preserved.
cards.apply: Record the program's observable output before the change and diff it against the agent's output on each commit, as CodeScene did with a frame-by-frame replay.
cards.result: The case study reports 300K lines of C refactored in three weeks for about $4,000 in tokens, with behavior checked mechanically.

evidence.note: CodeScene's published case study reports the line count, duration and token cost.

cards.title: Cut retrieval work and hydrate results in parallel to halve latency
cards.problem: Serial retrieval and result hydration put the full pipeline cost on every request's critical path.
cards.apply: Retrieve fewer candidates, fetch the per-result data in parallel instead of in sequence, and measure latency to what the user sees first rather than to the last byte.
cards.result: Uber reports a 50% cut in end-to-end Uber Eats search latency after these changes.

evidence.note: Uber reports the 50% latency reduction for its own search pipeline.

cards.title: Pair LLM judges with deterministic checks in one shared eval framework
cards.problem: Ad-hoc, per-team agent evals each use different judges and are not comparable across products.
cards.apply: Put every agent eval behind one reusable harness, and run deterministic rule checks wherever the answer can be verified, reserving the LLM judge for what rules cannot score.
cards.result: Evals become comparable across agents and less exposed to judge noise.

evidence.note: Based on Elastic's talk on moving from siloed evals to one framework.

cards.title: Invalidate dependent memories when a source fact changes
cards.problem: Long-term agent memory keeps serving facts that newer observations have made outdated.
cards.apply: Store provenance with each memory (which observation or memory it derives from), and when a source is corrected, mark every derived memory stale and re-derive or drop it.
cards.result: The agent stops acting on stale derived facts after an update.

evidence.note: Applies the PACMI paper's provenance-aware invalidation idea; no measured figure cited.

cards.title: Treat every MCP layer as an injection surface, not just user input
cards.problem: Adversarial instructions can arrive through tool schemas, tool outputs and protocol messages, not only the user prompt.
cards.apply: Sanitize and constrain tool descriptions and tool results as untrusted data, allowlist the MCP servers you connect, and test your agent against injections at each of the four layers.
cards.result: Fewer injection paths go untested, so hostile tool content is less likely to steer the agent.

evidence.note: COPEX names the four MCP layers where adversarial context enters; no measured result cited.

cards.title: Benchmark multi-agent debate against majority voting before shipping it
cards.problem: Multi-agent debate adds cost and latency, yet often fails to beat simple majority voting.
cards.apply: Run a majority-vote baseline over the same samples on your eval set, and keep debate only if it wins, with a verifier-aware step to pick the final answer.
cards.result: The paper claims debate helps only when it surfaces a correct answer and the readout verifies it, so you pay for it only where it wins.

evidence.note: The paper states debate often fails to beat majority voting.

cards.title: Validate your eval graders before hill-climbing on them
cards.problem: Optimizing an agent against an unchecked grader tunes it to the grader's mistakes.
cards.apply: Before iterating on prompts or tools, audit the grader against hand-labeled cases, then hill-climb only against the checked grader, as the claude-api plugin's build_eval and hill-climb commands do.
cards.result: Score gains reflect real improvement instead of grader quirks.

evidence.note: Based on Hamel Husain's description of the new tooling; no measured result.
